Transferred in March 1964 after losing his place to Alf Arrowsmith.

overview: Liverpool won the First Division in only their second season back in the top flight, ending a 17-year wait for the championship. Bill Shankly added Peter Thompson from Preston North End in August, giving the attack a regular left-wing partner for Ian Callaghan. Thompson played all 42 league matches; Kevin Lewis left for Huddersfield soon after his arrival.

An uneven start gave way to a powerful scoring campaign. Roger Hunt finished with 31 league goals and 33 in all competitive matches, while Ian St John scored 21 in the league. Alf Arrowsmith’s emergence added another 15 league goals, and Jimmy Melia moved to Wolves in March. Liverpool scored 92 league goals altogether, with Ron Yeats captaining a side built around the players Shankly had assembled during promotion and the return to the First Division.

The FA Cup ended in a 2–1 quarter-final defeat by Swansea Town at Anfield, but Liverpool recovered from a March league defeat at Fulham to win their next seven matches. The last of those, a 5–0 home win over Arsenal on 18 April, secured the title with three games remaining. Thompson scored twice. Liverpool finished four points ahead of Manchester United and qualified for their first European Cup campaign: promotion had been followed by a national championship within two years.

events.title: Peter Thompson joins from Preston
events.detail: The £37,000 signing became an ever-present in the league during his first Liverpool season.

events.title: Swansea end the FA Cup run
events.detail: Second Division Swansea Town won 2–1 at Anfield in the sixth round, the quarter-final stage.

events.title: Shankly’s first league championship
events.detail: Liverpool beat Arsenal 5–0 at Anfield to secure the title. Peter Thompson scored twice; Ian St John, Alf Arrowsmith and Roger Hunt also scored.

researchNotes: Top scorer means all competitive first-team matches: Hunt’s 33 comprises 31 league and two FA Cup goals. There was no Charity Shield appearance this season.

Jim Furnell’s Arsenal fee is £15,000 in LFChistory’s transfer register but £16,000 in the contemporary Daily Express transcription. The published transfer omits the fee rather than choosing between them.

The significant senior transfer list includes all four departures in LFChistory’s season register. John Sealey’s September 1963 move from Warrington Town is omitted as a developmental signing; he made only one subsequent Liverpool senior appearance.
No European or League Cup section is created because Liverpool did not participate in either competition. The 1964 Charity Shield belongs to the following season.
